moments.title: She can ask sensible questions now, and understands the terms
moments.summary: The speaker opens by saying she understands more, can actually ask sensible questions, and now recognises the terminology — and repeats that she feels more aware.
moments.evidence: I can actually ask sensible questions and before when I understand some terms, I almost importantly have something that I can go back to. I feel more aware, I just feel more aware.

moments.title: The book is what she can go back to when the brain fog takes the rest
moments.summary: She says the workbook is the part that lasts: with brain fog she expects to forget everything, and what matters is that the book is there to go back to.
moments.evidence: I think the book is really good because at the end of the day, I know with my brain fog, I'm going to forget everything. But the point is it's amazing that this is there to give, I mean to go back.

moments.title: The most fun part was being able to ask anything at all
moments.summary: Asked what the most fun part of the workshop was, she answers that it was being able to ask any question, and credits the facilitator with being consistently patient about answering them.
moments.evidence: What was the most fun part of this workshop? I think being able to ask any question and the fact that you've always been extremely patient about answering all.

moments.title: RESTRICTED — the speaker asks twice that this passage not be published
